claims.text: The Pulumi docs page at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists (link target of the 'Provider support policy' card on the support index page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi provides long-term security updates for some providers (the provider support policy page identifies which providers get long-term security updates).
Pulumi's provider version support policy focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers Pulumi maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page (/docs/support/provider-support-policy/) lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The Provider support policy page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`; it compares desired state against last recorded state.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.

Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name to form physical names, and this lets Pulumi replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement before deleting the old resource.
Auto-naming can be disabled per resource, and can be customized or disabled globally, per provider, or per resource type via project or stack configuration.

Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack for encrypting secrets, configurable to use a custom secrets provider; encrypting the same value in two stacks yields different encrypted strings.
`pulumi config set --secret` encrypts the value so it can be persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way, though some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.

Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in, enabled via a flag, command, or environment variable such as `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, and can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
Minor provider versions typically include new resources and features, performance improvements, and bug fixes without breaking changes.
In npm, the tilde operator (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates on eligible older versions are: AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/ for the listed providers.

The LTS branch of a covered provider ships High/Critical CVE security patches: fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

An LTS release of a Pulumi provider does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi (engine) they were frozen at unless security fixes prompt otherwise.
Under the provider support policy, exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.

When major version N+1 of a provider ships, it becomes the new N and the old N becomes the new LTS major; the old LTS major reaches end of life on the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major version is recommended.
Older majors than the LTS version of a covered provider receive no patches; if v3 is the newest release, v3 is N, v2 is N−1, and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) of a provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life provider versions (N−2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.

The Pulumi docs FAQ at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has a section 'What are the best practices for maintaining provider versions' (anchor #what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions).
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
